newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end higher but mood cautious.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end higher but mood cautious.

text.p: Swiss shares ended higher in quiet trading and on moderate volume on Monday, drawing strength from a firming tone in bonds and early advances on Wall Street.

But uncertainty about future developments dampened sentiment, dealers said, with U.S. indices already high and investors cautious ahead of U.S. producer prices and consumer prices data due on Wednesday and Thursday.
Dealers said the sagging U.S. dollar was not a factor in the market.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index ended up 15.6 points, or 0.41 percent, at 3,827.6 points, overcoming resistance at 3,825.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 6.20 points, or 0.25 percent, at 2,445.86 points.
Certificates of pharmaceutical company Roche led the actives list, ending up 30 Swiss francs at 9,740.
Insurer Swiss Re slid five francs to 1,383 francs before announcing after trading closed it was in talks to acquire a reinsurance unit from Italy's INA.

Dealers said the shares suffered on a profit warning by German competitor Muenchener Rueck. There also may have been switches from Swiss Re to insurer Zurich, a dealer said. Zurich stock jumped 1.43 percent to 354.

Union Bank of Switzerland bearers rose nine francs to 1,245. A dealer said UBS shares were sought ahead of a news conference it will hold on November 26. Traders think UBS may announce a restructuring as other Swiss banks have done.
CS Holding gave up 0.25 francs to 128.50.
Nestle was up five francs at 1,415.
Winterthur jumped 1.6 percent to 764. One dealer said the stock was making up for recent losses.
ABB added 11 francs, rising to 1,598. The company said it took over GEC Meters from Britain's General Electric.

Shares of second-tier industrial group Fischer ended up three percent at 1,300 francs on new buy recommendations. There was some aggressive buying in the stock, a dealer said. Danzas also continued its recent strong bias.

On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex), action in SMI futures was high with 10.670 contracts traded. This was due to roll-over transactions ahead of the Soffex expiry on Friday, dealers said.
A trader saw the expiry of SMI futures at around 3,850 points.
UBS options were in demand due to UBS's press conference.
